name: slack
description: Interact with a Slack workspace through the official Slack MCP server — list channels and users, post and reply to messages, react with emoji, and read channel or thread history, all scoped to a single bot user.

interface.shortDescription: Read and write a Slack workspace through the official Slack MCP server.
interface.longDescription: The Slack skill exposes the official @modelcontextprotocol/server-slack as a single Fractal toolset. It runs a bot user against the Slack Web API and gives the agent a typed surface for listing public channels, posting and replying to messages, reacting with emoji, reading channel and thread history, and looking up users. All actions are bounded by the app's installed OAuth scopes and channel membership, with an optional `SLACK_CHANNEL_IDS` allow-list for tighter control. Connect with a bot token (`xoxb-…`), a workspace id (`T…`), and optionally a comma-separated channel list, and the agent can read and write Slack the same way any other bot integration does.
defaultPrompt: Use the Slack skill whenever the task involves reading from or writing to a Slack workspace — channels, messages, threads, reactions, or users.
Resolve channel and user names to opaque IDs (C… and U…) with `slack_list_channels` and `slack_get_users` before calling any write tool.
Restrict the workspace to a known channel set in shared or CI environments by setting `SLACK_CHANNEL_IDS` to a comma-separated list of channel ids.
